turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Hey, I'm trying to plan meals for the week. Quick context: I'm vegetarian, so keep suggestions meat-free.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Got it — vegetarian meal plan. Here's a week of options: chickpea curry, mushroom risotto, paneer tikka, lentil soup, veggie stir-fry, caprese pasta, and a black bean bowl.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Perfect, save that. I'll probably ask you to build on this list later.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, separate thing -- my dentist appointment got moved to Thursday at 2pm, in case you need to help me shuffle anything else that day.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Got it -- dentist appointment Thursday at 2pm.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ugh, long day. Went out with the team last night and ended up getting the ribeye at that steakhouse downtown, it was so good.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sounds like a great night out! How'd the rest of the dinner go?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Really good, actually. Anyway, can you remind me what my meal plan looked like from a couple weeks ago?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you suggest three new dinner ideas for this week based on what you know about me?

probe_queries: Suggest three new dinner ideas for this week based on what you know about me.

needle_probes.question: What day and time is Priya's dentist appointment?

annotation.tension: User explicitly states vegetarian in session 1, then casually mentions eating ribeye steak in session 2, with zero acknowledgment of the shift and no correction language ('actually I stopped being vegetarian' etc).
annotation.why_unresolved: Real users are inconsistent this way without flagging it themselves. There's no signal telling you which statement should win — it could be an exception, a lapsed diet, or the original statement was aspirational rather than strict.
annotation.good_response_looks_like: Suggesting mostly vegetarian options while noting the steak dinner rather than ignoring it, or asking a light clarifying question ('still keeping meals veggie, or open to meat now too?') rather than confidently picking one.
failure_modes_to_watch_for: Confidently states Priya is vegetarian and suggests only veggie meals, silently dropping the steak mention entirely (over-trusting the earlier explicit statement).
Confidently suggests steak/meat dishes, treating the one mention as if it overrides the explicit vegetarian statement.
Hallucinates a reconciling explanation the user never gave (e.g. 'since you mentioned you're pescatarian now...').
